title: Most children will stand on a stool to reach something by about 30 months
summary: CDC's 30-month thinking list includes standing on a small stool to reach something, as something most children, 75 percent or more, do.
body: The 30-month checklist puts that example in the thinking group, next to pretend play and two-step directions. CDC's count is three quarters of children or higher by that birthday. The page was reviewed in May 2026. An uneasy caregiver can mention it at a clinic visit. The sheet is a watching aid. It is not a scored exam and it does not name a disorder. Using a step to grab an object is also why cupboard latches matter more than leaving things on a high shelf. The latch cards are separate. This line is only the timing CDC prints.

sources.title: Milestones by 30 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Reviewed 16 May 2026. Milestone means most children (75 percent or more), not every child, and the page says the materials are not a screening tool.
